title: Microsoft Teams: pop out the sign language interpreter video in meetings
summary: The roadmap description, dates and cited controls are supported. However, the assertion that IP video is the only documented meeting policy for interpreter video overlooks the broader video policies Microsoft documents; narrow that assertion before publishing.

claims.claim: IP video is the only documented meeting policy setting for interpreter video.
claims.quote: This setting controls both outgoing and incoming video for meetings and group calls that a user organizes or attends.
claims.fix: Replace 'The only meeting policy setting documented for interpreter video is IP video' with 'The accessibility guide documents IP video as a meeting policy setting for interpreter video'. Microsoft also documents Mode for IP video as controlling incoming and outgoing meeting video at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-audio-and-video; do not claim IP video is the only policy.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The accessibility guide ties the IP video setting to interpreters sharing their video feed.
claims.quote: Give sign language interpreters the ability to share IP video feed during Microsoft Teams meetings so they can communicate with users who are deaf or hard of hearing.

claims.claim: The accessibility guide gives Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Audio & video > IP video.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Meetings, and then select Meeting policies. Select the policy you want to modify. Go to the Audio & video section. Check that IP video is turned On, then select Save.
claims.fix: Keep the cited path, but add: 'The accessibility guide calls the setting IP video; the audio and video policy reference instead lists Mode for IP video and Video conferencing.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-audio-and-video, which uses those labels.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowIPVideo $true to allow video sharing.
claims.quote: [-AllowIPVideo <Boolean>] ... Determines whether video is enabled in a user's meetings or calls. Set this to TRUE to allow the user to share their video.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, guest-access bullet
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist tells readers to check has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Confirm that guest access is set up for external interpreters ... Controls rows: Whether the sign language interpreter pop-out is available to users; Whether interpreters can share an IP video feed in meetings.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet 'Confirm that guest access is set up for external interpreters, as the accessibility guide describes.' It directs readers to check guest access, which has no controls-table row.
